description:
## Goal

Resolve every callable reference exactly once through the ordinary lexical/expansion traversal, then retain its typed local or FunctionId identity through quote, macro execution, unquote, expansion, capture analysis, guards, and lowering. Source identifiers and qualified names exist only before resolution and for diagnostics or macro-visible display.

## Correct model

A module Namespace cannot identify local bindings. Local lexical identity is the pair of one typed SyntaxContext and the source identifier. One staged lexical environment and one set of scope operations begin in the existing expansion traversal: before values exist they record typed binding/classification by that key, and lowering realizes the same local keys to the existing ValueId. This is one authority across stages, not two algorithms sharing a key type. Do not add a LocalBindingId registry, parallel environment, quote-only name set, scanner, or side table.

SyntaxContext is structural and immutable. A source body begins with its typed function/source owner. Each macro expansion extends its parent context with the exact macro FunctionId and structural syntax address of the invocation. Child addresses follow explicit AST edges and sequence positions, not scheduling order, allocation order, a global counter, heap address, display text, or source span alone. Equal reproduction yields the same context; repeated and nested invocations remain distinct. Canonical output renders the typed owner and structural path, never raw World allocation numbers.

Executable map construction is the existing ordered `%{}` AST entry list. A raw runtime MAP is recursively inert quoted value data: AST-shaped tuples stored inside its keys or values do not expand, bind, capture, allocate generated functions, or establish execution order. This syntax/data boundary removes the old recursive raw-map walk and decoder sequencing whose storage order could change from ignored diagnostic metadata. Ordered map AST entries use the same explicit sequence-position addressing as other syntax; do not add a map comparator, map-key identity, snapshot, content hash, or map-only scope workaround.

Quote bodies are visited by that same binding traversal in an explicit template stage; unquote switches to the enclosing active stage. Quote-introduced binders and references share the invocation context supplied through `__CALLER__`, represented before execution as a typed context parameter rather than a provisional concrete context. Unquote preserves the inserted caller context. Fresh dynamically constructed syntax acquires the insertion context exactly once. Existing branch, clause, block, pattern, and lambda scope rules decide visibility and rebinding; the context distinguishes concordant names owned by different syntax. No later substitution, restamping, or repair pass exists.

A callable target is either unresolved source carrying its exact Namespace, SyntaxContext, and validated source-name shape, or Bound(FunctionId). The single lexical traversal resolves a visible local through the contextual environment; otherwise a known definition-owned function becomes Bound and a missing name remains definition-owned. Definition-owned unresolved calls never inspect a caller context. Preserve the existing ordinary rule that macro classification precedes local callable dispatch.

Keep the standard quoted AST shape and encode typed context/target in existing metadata. Bound(FunctionId) is authoritative even if a macro changes the visible head spelling. Its display head is arbitrary quoted data: never expand, decode as source, or use it for dispatch. Creating a new semantic target requires fresh unresolved metadata, not a display-string edit. Argument changes validate bound arity and never choose another overload by spelling. Unresolved heads are validated as supported source-name shapes at the quoted read/decode boundary, so guard and lowering paths never rely on unreachable shape assumptions.

World remains the one identity and namespace authority. Macro-call expansion constructs `Expansion(parent_context, exact_macro_FunctionId, structural_invocation_address)` before execution and projects it as part of the existing `ScopeSnapshot`-based `__CALLER__` value. Quote lowering reads that runtime field through ordinary lowering steps and emits it directly. The owning QuotedSourceHeap carries one shared World identity-domain token inherited by roots and subroots; it does not retain World. Bind the heap when compiler-owned identities first enter it, preserve or validate the domain during cross-heap transport, and reject malformed or foreign typed identities before probing World. Do not serialize World identity into every node or introduce a resource, namespace snapshot, runtime context side channel, fallback resolver, binding store, restamper, or compatibility path.

Executable scope parity is mandatory: clause, branch, cond, with, lambda, and pin handling reuse the existing lowering visibility rules. Bitstring size expressions read locals and never introduce binders. Macro arguments preserve caller syntax ownership, but their final binding/reference role is determined at insertion; merely passing an argument does not execute syntax, bind locals, record captures, or allocate generated functions. Only executed unquote and context-parameter holes participate in enclosing executable captures.

Structural addresses include the owning module path in the source tree, the source-item position, grouped function-clause position, and every intervening AST edge. Restarting a scope or entering a demanded module cannot reset away an enclosing structural address.

The quoted read boundary decodes one exclusive typed metadata classification. It validates ordinary calls, bare function references, explicit arity, supported unresolved heads, and resolved module aliases without consulting Bound display data. A Bound target still observes callable kind and interface readiness; retaining identity does not bypass macro-before-local classification or dependency observation. An unresolved target retains its persistent definition Namespace, never a transient namespace extended with heap-owned __ENV__ Splice values.

Identity publication binds the heap domain atomically with typed metadata construction. Cross-heap transport validates the domain, semantic equality distinguishes foreign domains, and canonical lowering retains typed identities instead of erasing them to undistinguished integer constants. Exact SourceVersion provenance remains independent of syntax ownership throughout.

## TDD signal

Use the cross-source macro case exposed during fz-tfn.53: App binds FutureMacros only as F, requires F.twice/1, and the provider macro quotes a call to its own double/1 helper. Prove both separate submission orders, driving only after the provider exists: each returns 42 and lowers the helper to the exact provider FunctionId. fz-tfn.46 owns the earlier requester-drive boundary, where today's unknown-import failure must become an observed exact ModuleInterface dependency and resume only when that provider arrives.

Prove all lexical ownership cases:

- A provider literal helper(41) ignores a same-spelled caller-local closure.
- A quote-introduced local = unquote(cb); local(41) selects that exact local.
- In the same expansion, unquote(caller_call) retains the caller's same-spelled local rather than the quote-local binding.
- A quote-local binding does not leak into the caller expression that follows the expansion.
- Repeated and nested invocations of the same macro cannot capture one another's locals.
- Generated lambdas capture exact contextual locals.
- Existing macro-before-local classification is unchanged.
- Missing provider names diagnose in the definition Namespace rather than borrowing caller locals.
- Fresh metadata resolves in its insertion context; copied metadata preserves ownership.

Prove that AST-shaped calls, bindings, and lambdas inside raw MAP data remain inert while repeated/nested calls in ordered `%{}` AST entries receive distinct contexts; reversing ignored raw-map metadata must mint no invocation or generated-function identity. Also prove copied metadata and head-only edits preserve a bound target; argument edits cannot retarget overloads; malformed Unresolved heads diagnose in ordinary and guard paths; malformed, out-of-range, and foreign-World targets diagnose without panic; arbitrary Bound display heads remain inert; and typed targets survive interpreter/native tuple-map transport. Assert typed lowered targets/captures, not rendered names. Preserve macro inspection/composition, semantic equality, deterministic unchanged/unrelated zero work, and byte-identical artifacts across allocation noise.

## Dependency order

1. Pin contextual references, exclusive metadata validation, structural addresses, and domain transport.
2. Finish staged expansion scope and capture rules against existing lowering behavior.
3. Replace quote reconstruction with generic serialization and ordinary holes; delete restricted QuoteLowerer, quote-only name/operator reconstruction, and template traversal by ordinary executable diagnostics.
4. Cut ordinary calls, function references, guards, and captures onto the same typed targets. Preserve fz-tfn.64 outcome and guard ownership; only change the lexical-key seam.
5. Run the ownership/composition matrix, three-door transport, exact reuse, and allocation-noise canonical/artifact tests; update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation.

## Strategy and deletion

Make the existing expansion traversal the one staged binding/classification authority while it walks syntax and classifies macros. It visits quote templates instead of skipping them, uses the same scope operations for ordinary and quoted syntax, and records contextual locals/captures and bound definition callables before macro execution. Serialize the already-classified quoted template generically, using ordinary lowering only for executed unquote and invocation-context holes. Delete the restricted QuoteLowerer reconstruction and its quote-only name/operator cases; ordinary executable diagnostics must not traverse template syntax. Generalize the existing lowering environment from String to the contextual lexical key and make it realize already-classified locals to ValueId; then delete downstream name-based local re-resolution and duplicate free-name authority. Collapse quote and ordinary call lowering onto the same typed target path.

Delete quoted_callable_name and every canonical module.function string used as post-resolution authority. Delete downstream generated-call module-path re-resolution and any workaround that adds provider names to caller namespaces or falls back from failed lexical lookup. Keep spelling and span only for unresolved source, diagnostics, and macro-visible display.

Update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation to state the single-resolution, syntax-context, and metadata contracts. Full focused/library/fixture/CLI gates, formatting, check, strict Clippy, deterministic reuse proof, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precede one commit and close. No temporary probe, duplicate traversal, compatibility path, or construction debris remains.
title: Keep callable identity through quoted source; delete canonical-name re-resolution
